newsitem.title: USA: Grounded tanker in Louisiana shuts Mississippi.
newsitem.headline: Grounded tanker in Louisiana shuts Mississippi.

text.p: A section of the lower Mississippi River was shut Friday after a tanker carrying low sulphur fuel oil grounded near Plaquemine, Louisiana, the Couast Guard said.
There was no immediate danger of a spill.
"At about 7:20 (CDT) last night, a tanker ran aground in the middle of the channel in the Mississippi River near Plaquemine, Louisiana," a Coast Guard spokesman told Reuters Friday.
The spokesman said the 678-foot tanker was carrying 375,000 barrels of light sulphur fuel oil destined for the Exxon refinery in Baton Rouge.
He said the Coast Guard was developing a salvage plan and he was not sure how long the section of the river between mile 205 and mile 227 would be closed.
The tanker was grounded a short distance from an 18-inch gas pipeline owned by Texaco, the spokesman said.
